summary: Grafana permission denied for Route Experiments metrics dashboards (internal users)
environment: prod (Grafana: primary; affected users across us-east and eu-west)
description:
Issue summary:
Several internal Redwood users (Console/Tooling + Telemetry teams) receive "Permission denied" when opening the new Route Experiments Grafana dashboards (guardrails + attribution drop rate). This is blocking on-call prep and beta readiness reviews.

Impact:
- Engineers cannot verify guardrail alerts/dashboards prior to beta expansion.
- Slows down triage of experiment issues because links from alert payloads point to dashboards that are not accessible.

Who is affected:
- Reported by Console/Tooling and Telemetry team members who are not in SRE groups.
- Example users: Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin (reported via DM to Observability).

What users see:
- Grafana banner: "Permission denied" / "You do not have permission to view this dashboard"
- Direct URL works for SRE users, fails for non-SRE.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Log into Grafana with an internal account not in SRE/Observability admin groups.
2) Open Route Experiments dashboard link from the rollout prep doc / Slack.
3) Observe permission denied.

Expected behavior:
- All engineering users in relevant org groups (eng-platform, eng-console-tooling, eng-telemetry) should have at least Viewer access to the dashboards used for route experiment operations.

Notes / context:
- Dashboards were added via Observability Pack rollout (see observability-pack#1934 and #1942).
- Folder-level permissions appear to be restricted to SRE-only.
- This is an internal access issue (not customer-facing).
comments: 2025-03-12 09:18 PT — Allison Grant (Reporter): Noticed multiple pings this morning that the Route Experiments dashboards are inaccessible to Console & Tooling. This will block the propagation lag game day and beta readiness checks. Can we fix folder ACLs and document the expected access path?

2025-03-12 09:42 PT — Aisha Bello (Assignee): Confirmed. Repro’d with my non-SRE test account: permission denied at folder level. The dashboards are under the "SRE / Guardrails" folder, which is restricted to SRE + Observability Admin groups.

2025-03-12 10:05 PT — Caleb Johnson: +1. I can’t open the attribution drop rate dashboard linked from the alert rule. Suggest moving these to a shared "Platform / Experiments" folder or adding Viewer access for eng-platform + eng-telemetry groups.

2025-03-12 10:31 PT — Aisha Bello: Proposed change: keep dashboards in current folder, but add Viewer permissions for groups: eng-platform, eng-console-tooling, eng-telemetry-analytics. Will also add a short Confluence note for "How to request access" and update the runbook link section so on-call knows where to go.

2025-03-12 11:20 PT — Aisha Bello: Implemented folder ACL update in Grafana: added Viewer access for eng-platform + eng-console-tooling + eng-telemetry-analytics. Verified with 2 users (Chloe Martin, Logan Wright) that the dashboards now load. Remaining issue: some users still can’t see folder in search unless they have org-level "Viewer" in Grafana (separate setting).
2025-03-12 12:02 PT — Allison Grant: Confirmed dashboards load for me now. Thanks. Can we capture the org-level Grafana role requirement in docs so we don’t keep re-triaging this?

2025-03-13 09:11 PT — Aisha Bello: Doc fix shipped: added a short section to the Experiment Health Dashboards spec explaining required Grafana roles + group mapping, and added "Access" step to the experiment assignment debugging runbook. Also posted a note in #eng-sre to route future requests through internal-support with the user’s Grafana org + groups.
2025-03-13 09:28 PT — Allison Grant: Great. Marking resolved.
root_cause: Grafana folder-level ACLs for the newly added Route Experiments dashboards were restricted to SRE/Observability admin groups, preventing non-SRE engineering groups from viewing dashboards referenced by runbooks/alerts.
resolution: Updated Grafana folder ACLs to grant Viewer access to eng-platform, eng-console-tooling, and eng-telemetry-analytics groups. Added documentation clarifying required Grafana org role and how to request access.
workaround: Temporarily ask an SRE/Observability Admin to screenshot/export panels for reviews (no longer needed after ACL update).
